brief: The viewer observes a vast, subterranean chamber where millennia of architectural and artistic history are disintegrating. Fragments of carved stone and patinated bronze statuary hang and shift in slow, random bursts of asymmetrical collapse. As the material gives way, the ongoing process dramatically reveals intricate, geometric patterns etched deep into the rock and debris, giving the sense of peering into a forgotten fault line. The colors are rich and earthy—deep oxides of bronze mixing with the cool grays and reds of compressed earth and carved marble. The entire landscape is designed to look perpetually dynamic, conveying the ceaseless, grinding march of erosion and time, which serves as the sole visible force in the piece.
